title: Send Analytics and inspect it in the Dashboard
lead: An Analytics collector listens to player events and sends playback data to Bitmovin. Inspect collected data in Bitmovin Dashboard under Observability. The app’s local state and QoE readouts help explain the playback currently on screen.

rows: Player Lab Web and native apps
Change settings or playback actions, then inspect player state and applied code.
Collect supported player events and playback context for the selected Analytics license.
Select the license, period and filters to inspect audience and playback quality.

blocks.text: Find a playback in the Dashboard

items: Play a video in an app configured for Analytics. Note the setting, source, device and playback time. In the Web app, also check the Analytics collection notice.
Sign in to Bitmovin Dashboard and open Observability. Select the same Analytics license used by the collector.
Choose a period containing your playback. Check the displayed time zone, then narrow the view with content or browser filters.
Find the playback through Plays or Latest Sessions under Audience. Use Quality of Experience to inspect Video Startup Time or Rebuffering Percentage.
Investigate failures through Top Errors or the session details. Match the playback and time when comparing the Dashboard with the app’s event log.

blocks.caption: Official Bitmovin demo screen showing the license, period, Global Filters and Video Title selectors. Values are dummy data. This older screen uses an Analytics menu label and layout that may differ from the current Dashboard. Source: the official sandbox article linked below. © Bitmovin.

blocks.text: You need access to the selected Analytics license in the Dashboard. Playing the public demo does not grant access to its destination account. To inspect your own data, configure your Analytics license in a local app. A collection notice or browser-local value alone does not establish that data reached the collector backend.

items: Open the Web app, choose VOD HLS or your own finite source, and start playback with Play. Read Player state and the QoE metrics below the player.
Seek with the player control. Compare Seek/Seeked in the event log with the seek time readout; live sources use TimeShift/TimeShifted instead.
Pause and resume. A deliberate pause does not count as rebuffering in this readout. A real StallStarted/StallEnded after playback begins increases its interruption count.
When comparing a changed configuration, open Show applied configuration code and copy the applied settings. Draft edits are not included. Load the same source again for a new measurement.

blocks.text: QoE means Quality of Experience. This panel computes values from the current player’s events. Its population and definitions differ from collected Analytics in the Dashboard.

rows: SourceLoaded to the first Playing event. Waiting before a manual Play can contribute; this is not the Analytics VIDEO_STARTUPTIME definition.
Stall time / (playing time + stall time) after startup. Manual pauses and initial buffering are excluded.
Number of Error events received by the current session, rather than the number of affected viewers.
Latest Seek or TimeShift request to its completion event.
Device wall clock minus the playback wall-clock timestamp; requires usable source timing such as HLS Program Date Time (PDT).
The SDK lowlatency.getLatency() value: distance from the live edge, rather than from real time.

blocks.text: A dash or needs PDT is not zero latency. QoE latency fields can retain their last valid value if timing becomes unavailable, so also check Player state for the current source.
Use events to explain a change

The event log includes SourceLoaded, Play, Playing, Paused, Seek, TimeShift, StallStarted and Error with local timestamps. New events appear first, with up to 80 lines. Frequent TimeChanged events update the readouts but are not listed in the log.

A new source load, source unload or player destruction resets the session measurements. Switching only the theme or UI keeps the same player measurements. At playback end, final totals stop increasing. Start a fresh load before comparing another trial.

The public Pages app also sends Analytics when configured. Its aggregate-query panel is hidden because Pages does not run a server that can hold an account API key. Use the Dashboard for routine inspection, and use local queries or the Query API when you need a custom aggregate.
